## Oriole and cloves  
China, Qing dynasty (1644- 1911), 18th century Keri (silk tapestry), hanging scroll, 72.3 x 43.6 cm Collector's seal: Lantang shanw Gift of Dr Lam Kwok Pun HKUT.2008.1677  
With a pinkish beak and smooth colourful feathers, the oriole on this silk tapestry is shown leaning forward and singing. Clove blossoms woven in red and blue wefts with subtle gradations evoke the warmth and vitality of spring. Because cloves bloom in spring, they are thought to be auspicious and bring all growth and prosperity. This work employs the behaviour (twisted coloured thread) technique, in which two or three coloured threads are entwined to form a single polychrome strand. Hêhuanian was widely adopted by kori weavers during the Qing dynasty, particularly in the production of kori depicting bird feathers in white and grey, such as the jaw of the oriole on this tapestry.
